title: review an IAM change using supported policy analysis
input: The security owner selects the relevant principal, resource and proposed IAM binding.
action: Policy Intelligence's supported tools analyze or recommend policy changes using available policy and usage evidence. Recommendations require owner review; unsupported evidence or unused permissions must be interpreted carefully.
output: The administrator applies the approved least-privilege change through the actual IAM policy interface.
check: Test permitted workflows and denied operations after the change and retain a rollback policy.

title: route approved enterprise egress through a security service edge provider
input: The network owner selects supported SSE integration and the NCC Gateway connectivity design.
action: Secure Access Connect connects supported security service edge products to NCC Gateway for security processing and internet egress. The configured SSE provider applies its inspection policy; the connector establishes the eligible path.
output: The enterprise application reaches the allowed internet destination through the selected gateway and security-provider path.
check: Test denied destinations, routing, return traffic and provider failure behavior before enabling the egress design.

title: host a controlled source repository for a release pipeline
input: The maintainer defines repository access, branch controls and the approved build integration.
action: Secure Source Manager provides supported managed source-repository capabilities under its configured access boundary. Developers push reviewed changes; the connected runner performs build and deployment operations separately.
output: The pipeline checks out the accepted commit and creates the versioned release artifact.
check: Verify repository visibility, branch policy, build credentials and history preservation before enabling production releases.

title: permit only approved outbound web destinations for a workload
input: The network owner configures the workload's proxy path and approved URL or identity conditions.
action: Secure Web Proxy evaluates supported outbound HTTP or HTTPS requests against its configured policy and permitted inspection settings. It allows or denies the proxy request; the destination application processes allowed business traffic.
output: The workload reaches an approved external API while prohibited web destinations are denied.
check: Test proxy usage, bypass prevention, TLS behavior and denied destinations before accepting the egress policy.

title: publish an approved deployment solution for project users
input: The platform owner selects a supported solution, deployment parameters and permitted catalog audience.
action: Service Catalog exposes the approved solutions to authorized users under its configured catalog scope. The selected deployment workflow provisions resources; the catalog is the discovery and governance entry point.
output: The developer chooses the permitted solution and deploys it through the actual authorized provisioning path.
check: Verify audience access, template version, generated resources and denied unapproved solutions before publication.

title: apply custom request logic at a supported load-balancing extension point
input: The application owner selects the supported extension type and its allowed request modifications.
action: Service Extensions invokes configured supported extension logic at the chosen traffic-processing point. The extension can inspect or modify supported request or response fields; the backend still performs the business operation.
output: The load-balanced backend receives the permitted resulting request and returns its response through the configured path.
check: Test extension timeouts, failure policy, field changes and backend authorization before enabling the extension.

title: respond to an account-relevant cloud service incident
input: The operator selects the project, affected resources and the incident window.
action: Service Health presents supported service-impact information relevant to the configured scope. The notification or status identifies a cloud incident; operators must correlate it with the application's actual affected requests.
output: The workload owner activates its approved recovery or communication procedure when the incident affects the application.
check: Verify resource impact and real application recovery rather than equating provider incident closure with business recovery.

title: publish a managed API service configuration for permitted consumers
input: The API producer defines the service configuration, supported checks and consumer onboarding requirements.
action: Service Infrastructure supplies foundational management and control capabilities for supported service producers. The API runtime integrates applicable service control checks and reporting; the producer backend executes the actual customer operation.
output: The producer enables the approved consumer project and serves requests under its configured authentication and quota policy.
check: Test consumer activation, denied requests, quota checks and runtime reporting with the actual API implementation.

title: enable a required API in an approved project
input: The project owner identifies the required service, permissions and deployment prerequisites.
action: Service Usage manages supported API enablement and service-use configuration for the project. Enabling an API makes its supported resource operations available under IAM; it does not create the application resource itself.
output: The deployment role creates the approved resource after the API is enabled and effective permissions are confirmed.
check: Check project selection, API dependencies and actual resource creation before marking the setup complete.

title: boot a protected application host with verified integrity settings
input: The platform owner selects a supported Shielded VM image and the required boot-security settings.
action: Shielded VMs supplies supported protections such as secure boot, virtual TPM and integrity monitoring. The guest application executes normally on the VM; configured protections provide platform integrity evidence rather than application-level authorization.
output: The service owner deploys the approved application and inspects integrity events during host changes.
check: Test image compatibility, boot settings, baseline changes and application recovery before accepting the host configuration.
